title: Contemporaneous reporting corroboration — depth 1
summary: Recursive target comparing observations made by The Verge, VICE Motherboard, NBC News, and official statements.

unresolved: The complete corpus was not forensically validated by these reports.
Article screenshots and outbound links still require local preservation and hashing.

notes: The Verge and VICE corroborate the event, extraction workflow, screenshots, and apparently novel posted media.
Their reports did not claim a complete forensic authentication of every file.
This distinction is recorded as verification scope, not a fabricated-source classification.

data.research_question: Which observations were independently made in July 2022, and which conclusions remained outside the reporting's verification scope?
objectives: Build a statement matrix for archive existence, screenshots, novel images, tool identity, agency awareness, and corpus authentication.
Preserve publication timestamps and source-to-source references.
Do not treat absent checksums as affirmative evidence of fabrication.
Do not overstate novelty or agency awareness as blanket file validation.
hypotheses: Contemporaneous sources corroborate the event and workflow more strongly than the entire corpus.
A scoped evidence matrix resolves apparent conflict around the word verified.
excluded_sources: commentary that does not link the underlying reporting

workflow.next_action: Capture the articles, outbound links, screenshots, and quoted statements; hash each capture and map every observation to its originating source.
